what: Two real agent runs of 12-13 September 2026, redacted for the repository. The raw session files stay in scratch and are never committed: they carry the absolute path of the machine they ran on, the operator's account name, and the harness's session, prompt and request identifiers.
redacted_by: labs/session06_assets/session06_agent.py -- transcript_rules() is the rule, redact()/redact_text() apply it, check_redaction() re-runs the proof. The build script that digests the raw files lives in scratch beside them, because its inputs cannot be committed; it imports the rules from this module rather than restating them.
relation_to_Lec09_transcripts: labs/Lec09_Agent_Lab/transcripts/ holds the same two runs TRUNCATED to 400 characters per tool result. These copies are REDACTED instead: identity is removed and content is kept. Two caps remain and are recorded per result rather than applied silently -- 20000 characters, fifty times the Lec09 copies -- and three results that were downloaded bytes echoed to the terminal are elided with their length and sha256 rather than carried as base64.
redaction_rule: Two passes. (1) Structural: the digest is rebuilt from the raw rows and the identity-bearing fields are never copied -- uuid, parentUuid, sessionId, session_id, promptId, requestId, request_id, leafUuid, sourceToolAssistantUUID, id, signature, cwd, gitBranch, userType, entrypoint, container, messaging_socket_path, memory_paths, apiKeySource, tool_use_id, parent_tool_use_id. (2) Textual: every surviving string is rewritten by the ordered substitutions below, most specific first, so a scratch path can never fall through to a generic rule.

substitutions.why: the folder the recorded run worked in
the harness's project slug, which spells a whole absolute path with dashes
a home directory on any other machine
a home directory on a shared filesystem, which is under neither /u nor /home
the account name anywhere else: a bare word, or a segment of a path on a shared filesystem
API message, tool-use and request identifiers

rules_added_after_the_first_pass: The harness writes a copy of every session under .claude/projects/<slug>, where the slug spells a whole absolute path with its slashes turned into dashes. It is not path-shaped, so no rule about paths caught it.
A shell PATH echoed by `which` named a home directory on a shared filesystem, under neither /u nor /home.
Both were found by running the proof, not by reading the rules.
kept_deliberately: Paths of the form /tmp/<filename> naming a file the agent itself created during the run, for example /tmp/hic04_acs.xlsx. They carry no account, machine or session identity, and removing them would hide what the agent did.

proof.note: the account-name check uses the account running it, so this proof was run by the operator who produced the files

row_schema.prompt: a prompt typed by the person: {n, text}
row_schema.attachment_note: a screenshot handed back to the model, as the harness recorded it
row_schema.thinking: one assistant thinking block, its cryptographic signature removed
row_schema.tool_use: {n, name, input} -- the call the model asked for
row_schema.tool_result: {is_error, chars, content}; chars is always the FULL length before any cap, capped_at appears when content was cut, and elided/sha256 appear when the result was downloaded bytes rather than text
row_schema.turn_usage: one row per API request, not per streamed block: {turn, model, input_tokens, cache_creation_input_tokens, cache_read_input_tokens, output_tokens, thinking_tokens}
row_schema.result: the harness's own closing summary: duration, cost, total usage
